Assessed Claim: Buyer is Berkshire Partners LLC, a Boston-based private equity investment firm acting through its funds; majority control buyer, with the Permira funds (and, per S22, management) retaining significant minority stakes. Not a multi-mandate consortium acting as one buyer.
Stated market condition: fast growth of the Sub-Saharan data centre infrastructure market and growing demand for internet and cloud services (Berkshire MD quote; Bloomberg framing).
Rivals Considered: Deal driven by seller exit timing alone (SM-08/SI-07) with market growth incidental.

Assessed Claim: Berkshire had deployable committed fund capital (sponsor mandate). Plausible given archetype; no retrieved source names the fund, vintage or commitment.
Rivals Considered: Co-investor or balance-sheet capital rather than a committed fund.
Process / Discriminating Test: Proposed: identify the Berkshire fund vehicle and vintage from filings (e.g. vehicle behind BPESAL V2 S.a r.l.). [test: NOT_RUN]

Assessed Claim: Financial ownership-value thesis: a PE sponsor with no operating data-centre business to combine takes majority control of the leading sub-Saharan interconnection-rich colocation platform to capture growth of the platform and realise value on exit, independent of strategic combination.
Rivals Considered: Strategic combination motive (BM-02 in-market expansion or BM-11 consolidation) via an existing Berkshire operating portfolio company; BM-01 geographic entry of Berkshire's portfolio into Africa.
Process / Discriminating Test: Hoop: does the buyer have an operating data-centre platform in South Africa that the target could be combined with? None found in any source (S19 lists only US-centred digital infrastructure activity). Straws: (a) sponsor archetype; (b) growth-capture framing, not synergy framing; (c) management continuity and standalone growth plan; (d) seller rollover typical of sponsor-to-sponsor secondary. Hoop passed and several independent straws present. [test: PASS]
Terminal Motive?: N (non-terminal; R37 satisfied via C10 value mechanism and ownership lever)
Terminal Rule Check: R37 PASS: BM-23 not sole motive-grade driver; supported VM-07 (E1) with ownership lever: Majority control of an ecosystem-rich platform directing growth capex (30MW to 60MW) and exit timing

Assessed Claim: Seller (Permira funds) sells a majority but remains a significant investor: partial monetisation with retained participation.
Rivals Considered: Full exit blocked by price gap, with rollover as a valuation bridge rather than a seller objective.

Assessed Claim: Fund-life realisation: Permira backed the MBO in December 2014, so about four years into its hold at signing; realisation plausible but fund term and vintage not sourced.
Rivals Considered: SM-10 valuation-window timing; SM-04 as the dominant objective.
Process / Discriminating Test: Proposed: identify the Permira fund holding Teraco and its term/investment period. [test: NOT_RUN]

Assessed Claim: Valuation-window timing: seller sought a sale when valuations were judged attractive. Consistent with a sourced sale process but no discriminating evidence.
Process / Discriminating Test: Proposed: compare entry multiple with contemporaneous DC multiples; entry value undisclosed. [test: NOT_RUN]

Assessed Claim: Formal sale process: Permira was reported in November 2018 to be working with an adviser to find a buyer; Torch Partners acted as sell-side adviser on the majority sale.
Process / Discriminating Test: Named sell-side adviser engaged AND independent pre-signing report of a buyer search: both present. [test: PASS]

Assessed Claim: Competitive auction with multiple bidders: no evidence of other bidders found.

Network and ecosystem density effects: the buyer states Teraco's positioning rests on its 'highly interconnected ecosystems'; Teraco lists five core ecosystems and hosts NAPAfrica, Africa's largest IXP. This is the supported value mechanism with an ownership lever for R37.
Rivals Considered: Plain capacity growth with fixed-cost absorption (VM-03.2), with ecosystem incidental.

Assessed Claim: Scarcity rent capture from an interconnection hub (largest African IXP) that rivals cannot readily replicate.
Rivals Considered: Competitive new supply erodes rents (see AT-07).
Process / Discriminating Test: Proposed: compare Teraco pricing/margins with non-IXP South African colocation peers in 2018-2019. [test: NOT_RUN]

Assessed Claim: Multiple arbitrage: buy below expected exit multiple. Entry value undisclosed (pre-deal range $600m to $1bn including debt was an expectation only).
Rivals Considered: Value creation from EBITDA and capacity growth, not multiple expansion.
Process / Discriminating Test: Proposed: verified entry EV/EBITDA versus exit (S15 values Teraco at about $3.5bn in 2022); exit data is hindsight and not used to define the ex-ante thesis. [test: NOT_RUN]

Assessed Claim: Operating capacity acquired: five facilities (Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban) with 30MW installed critical power load (operating metric).
Ecosystem / interconnected community: more than 450 clients across five core ecosystems (telecoms, managed service providers, content, enterprise, financial services).
Connectivity/interconnection assets: host of NAPAfrica internet exchange point, ranked top-15 globally in 2018.
Customer relationships: more than 450 clients incl. global internet companies; clients reported to include China Telecom Global and AWS.
Development pipeline: stated ambition to double to 60MW over the next few years (development target, not operating capacity); specific pipeline sites at signing not evidenced.
Rivals Considered: Ambition met by brownfield expansion of existing campuses only.
Process / Discriminating Test: Proposed: identify land/pipeline held at signing (JB4 site appears only in Nov 2020). [test: NOT_RUN]

Assessed Claim: Acquisition of control (majority stake) of the whole company; not a 100% acquisition.
Partial sell-down: the incumbent sponsor sells a majority while retaining a significant stake.
Acquisition debt (LBO). Only the aggregator flags LBO; no primary financing disclosure retrieved.
Rivals Considered: Equity-funded acquisition with existing opco debt left in place.
Process / Discriminating Test: Proposed: lender announcements or holdco financial statements for 2019. [test: NOT_RUN]

Assessed Claim: Standalone / one-off at announcement: no repeat acquisition programme evidenced; growth path described as organic capacity doubling.
Rivals Considered: PG-01 platform for a pan-African buy-and-build.
Process / Discriminating Test: Hoop: any announced add-on strategy? None. Straw: stated organic build route. Post-close check OU-07: no add-ons found (not used to define). [test: PASS]

Assessed Claim: Ex-ante intent to preserve Teraco as a standalone platform under its own management and brand, funded for growth.
Rivals Considered: II-03 selective functional integration with a Berkshire portfolio company.
Process / Discriminating Test: Hoop: an integration target exists in the buyer group? None found. Straw: management continuity statement dated at signing. [test: PASS]
Terminal Rule Check: R38 PASS: intent source dated 2019-01-24, before any closing (closing required regulatory approval)

Assessed Claim: Financial / governance-only ownership: buyer intends to govern and fund rather than integrate operationally.
Rivals Considered: Active operating involvement by the sponsor.
Terminal Rule Check: R38 PASS: intent source dated 2019-01-24, before any closing (closing required regulatory approval)

Assessed Claim: Capex follow-through: in November 2020 Berkshire-backed Teraco announced a $250m JB4 build (phase 1 about 19MW), funded by shareholders and lenders. Consistent with stated growth-investment plan (C04/C22); does not upgrade BM-23 to E2 because BM-23 is E3 not E1.

Exit / realised-return outcome: Berkshire and Permira agreed on 2022-01-03 to sell a majority of their stakes to Digital Realty (about 55%, about $1.7bn, Teraco valued about $3.5bn), completed 2022-08-01, retaining minority stakes. Corroborates the financial ownership-value thesis (consistent, not upgrading beyond E3).
Add-on sequence under Berkshire: none found.
Kill condition: new colocation supply or hyperscaler self-build in South Africa erodes the interconnection/scarcity position paid for.
Rivals Considered: Hyperscaler entry raises demand for neutral interconnection (supports thesis).
Process / Discriminating Test: Proposed: Teraco utilisation and pricing 2019-2021 versus new entrant capacity. [test: NOT_RUN]

Assessed Claim: Kill condition: price paid exceeds capturable value. Untestable ex ante because entry price undisclosed.
Geographic entry of Berkshire into sub-Saharan Africa. Possible, but for a financial sponsor no evidence that geographic presence per se was the purpose.
Process / Discriminating Test: Proposed: Berkshire statements of an Africa or emerging-markets digital-infrastructure strategy pre-2019. [test: NOT_RUN]

Assessed Claim: Ecosystem acquisition. Fits the stated 'interconnected ecosystems' rationale but is a candidate concept; coded instead as RO-15 plus VM-07 and logged as residual RS08.

Competition-law feasibility: the deal was subject to regulatory / Competition Commission approval (S01, S22). Approval decision, date and instrument details were not retrievable, so R27 cannot be satisfied.
Capital-deployment pressure distorting price: no indicators available (price, premium undisclosed).
No dated catalyst evidenced. Fund hold-period maturity undated; Microsoft Azure South Africa regions launched 2019-03-06, after signing, so cannot be the signing catalyst.
Competitive threat from new entrants as a driver of seller timing: no evidence retrieved.
